stock.counterargument: The honest counterargument is the sample: this process has not been shown to work, and a single ranking position is not evidence about one company.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +102.0%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $40.42 on the decision date.
risks: The share count is from 2026-06-30, 106 days older than the price, so the market capitalisation carries that staleness.
The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-06-30, 106 days before the decision date.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-10-14.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2025-11-06) plus 364 days

stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
stock.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

By working through this quiz, you’ll revisit how to create a PyQt app, arrange widgets with layout managers, build main windows and dialogs, connect signals to slots, and structure a GUI calculator with the Model-View-Controller pattern.

stories.excerpt: Defense Secretary Hegseth's announcement of a livestreamed execution elicited reactions of disgust and condemnation from some faith leaders and politicians. But within his church, it's not an outlier.
stories.lead: It is not clear if the public execution of the man behind the Fort Hood attack will be livestreamed, as Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said it would be late last week. When asked about it on Tuesday, President Trump said, "We're looking at it," and Vice President JD Vance has stated that he would not watch it, raising doubts about whether it would happen. stories.title: What's going on between Kelly Clarkson and a Brooklyn store bird?
stories.excerpt: The Since U Been Gone singer claims she was "looked at as if I couldn't afford" an item in the store.
stories.lead:
A boutique store called Art of Play in Brooklyn has found itself at the centre of a social media storm, after Grammy winner Kelly Clarkson complained that they would not let her buy a singing and dancing mechanical bird that was on the wall.

The Since U Been Gone singer claimed she was "looked at as if I couldn't afford" the bird - which she said had a price tag of $15,000 (£11,000).

Art of Play has defended how it treated the star, saying the wooden bird is permanently attached to the wall and is not for sale.

stories.title: White House defends new press secretary amid questions about her legal credentials
stories.excerpt: Katie Zacharia does not appear to be registered to the legal bar in any state where she has lived.
stories.lead:
The White House is defending its new press secretary, Katie Zacharia, as she faces scrutiny over her legal credentials.

President Donald Trump described Zacharia as an attorney when announcing her appointment last week. She has referred to herself as a lawyer.

But when she was asked on Tuesday by a reporter in which state she had passed the bar exam required to be an attorney in the US, she said standing alongside the president: "When I moved to China."

stories.title: Musk says US government may be behind slowdown of Ukraine drone speeds
stories.excerpt: Ukraine says Starlink access has improved but it is still facing speed limits which are disrupting its battlefield "missions".
stories.lead:
Elon Musk has suggested that the US government may be behind restrictions on the speed at which some of Ukraine's weapons can travel and stay connected to SpaceX's Starlink internet network.

Starlink is a vital tool allowing Kyiv to guide drones to Russian targets and also protect its own skies, but on Tuesday night Ukraine said unexpected new speed limits were disrupting its battlefield missions.

An adviser to President Volodymyr Zelensky said he believed the restrictions were not a coincidence and were related to the latest strains between Kyiv and Washington.

stories.title: Tech market sell-off deepens amid fears over US inflation and AI debt
stories.excerpt: Chip makers and tech investors such as Samsung and SoftBank plunge as global investors fret over potential interest rate hikes Business news – live updates Larry Elliott: the global economy is muddling through. But a storm is coming An accelerating sell-off of AI-linked shares has hit global…
stories.lead:
An accelerating sell-off of AI-linked shares has hit global markets, as fears over rising inflation and future interest rate hikes spooked traders already wary of the heavily indebted sector.

South Korea’s benchmark Kospi 200 index, which is heavily skewed towards the companies that make memory chips, fell more than 8% overnight to a six-month closing low, triggering circuit breakers that brought trading to a halt at various points.

Some of those semiconductor stocks, such as SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics, plunged nearly 11% and 9.5%, respectively. The index closed at a six-month low, down 8.1%.

stories.title: UK economy sees surprise growth in August ahead of Healey's first Budget
stories.excerpt: The uptick helped the economy grow by 0.7% over the three months to August, official figures show.
stories.lead:
The UK's economy recorded surprise growth in August despite the impact of rising energy prices and borrowing costs.

Official figures showed the economy expanded by 0.1% in the month, defying analysts' expectations of a slight contraction.

It means the economy grew by 0.7% in the three months to August, and follows an upgrade to this year's forecast for the UK economy from global watchdog the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

stories.title: Anthropic flags revenue surge to investors ahead of stock market debut
stories.excerpt: It comes as some investors have become concerned about the amount of money being spent on AI infrastructure.
stories.lead:
Artificial intelligence (AI) giant Anthropic saw its revenue surge by 45% to $16.8bn (£12.7bn) in the three months to the end of September, the BBC understands.

The figures were revealed by the Claude-developer in a briefing for prospective investors on Wednesday as it lays the groundwork for a stock market listing, which is expected to take place before the end of the year.

It comes as some tech stocks, including firms that make the chips and other hardware that power data centres, have fallen in recent days over concerns about the hundreds of billions of dollars being spent on AI infrastructure.

stories.title: Harvard Men's Water Polo Sweep NWPC Weekly Awards
stories.excerpt: Crimson trio of Strauser, Carrington, Price honored by conference.
stories.lead:
CAMBRIDGE, Mass. -- Harvard men's water polo swept the NWPC's weekly awards by taking home the player of the week, rookie of the week and defensive player of the week honors after a 2-0 weekend with wins over Brown and MIT.

Junior Dean Strauser (Calabasas, Calif.) earned his first NWPC Player of the Week nod of the season after leading the Crimson with nine points on the weekend. He started with two goals in a critical win over Brown on Saturday and followed up with a seven-point, four-goal, three-assist performance to beat MIT.
